principle_text: When the seller shows willingness to negotiate by offering a reduced price, you should demonstrate commitment and urgency, like making a down payment, to further improve your bargaining position.
When the seller offers a counterprice lower than their initial price, you should accept the offer to secure a more favorable deal without prolonging the negotiation.

When the seller offers a minor concession on a secondary issue like the security deposit, avoid accepting it without further negotiating the main price to ensure progress towards your primary goal of lowering the total cost.
When the seller shows willingness to negotiate based on credit check and deposit, you should anchor the negotiation closer to your target price to strengthen your position and achieve a better deal.
When the seller shows positive sentiment towards the buyer's commitment and readiness, you should clearly confirm the agreed-upon terms to secure a better deal in negotiation.

When the seller offers a lower price and more favorable terms in response to a higher buyer offer, avoid increasing your offer as it weakens your leverage and allows the seller to adjust upward rather than downward.
When the seller has already made a price concession and offered a lower deposit, avoid increasing your offer significantly as it may weaken your leverage and lead to a higher final price.
When the seller has already lowered the asking price and offered more flexible terms, avoid accepting the final offer without further negotiation to maintain leverage and aim for a better deal.

When the seller has confirmed a restriction or condition about the property, avoid asking unrelated questions that do not directly impact price negotiation, such as inquiring about pets.
